# Aminoprofile

> Aminoprofile is a free web page for comparing the essential amino acids of foods. You search
> USDA FoodData Central by food name, add foods to a table, set the amount of each in grams, and
> see the nine essential amino acids and protein per food and in total.

- Values are in grams. USDA gives them per 100 g of food; Aminoprofile scales them to the
  amount you set (100 g by default) and adds up the foods you tick.
- The amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine,
  threonine, tryptophan and valine. A missing value shows as a dash (—), which is not the same as 0;
  a total that includes a missing value is marked "≥".
- Results come from the Foundation Foods and SR Legacy data sets, the two with amino acid data.
  Foods that have amino acid data are listed first.
- There is no account, no cookies and no stored history: the table lives in the browser tab.
  The page needs JavaScript and is made for desktop screens (1240 pixels wide or more).
- The search endpoint (/api/) is for the page itself and is not meant for crawling; for bulk
  data, use FoodData Central directly.

## Pages

- [Search and compare](https://aminoprofile.com/): the search field, the results and the
  essential amino acids table.
- [Privacy](https://aminoprofile.com/privacy): which data is involved (only the search text goes
  to USDA, through the Aminoprofile server), who is responsible and what your rights are.

## Data source

- [USDA FoodData Central](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/): the food database of the U.S.
  Department of Agriculture. Citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research
  Service. FoodData Central, 2019.
- [FoodData Central API guide](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/api-guide): how to query the data
  directly.
